Analytics data points (fields) reference

Fields are the building blocks of analytics in Shopify. They're the individual data points you can select, filter, and group when creating reports. Fields come in 2 types:

  • Metrics are numbers you measure, such as net sales, orders, or sessions. They answer "how much" or "how many."
  • Dimensions are attributes you group by, such as product title, day, or traffic source. They answer "which" or "what kind."

This reference lists all available fields organized by category. Use the description and notes to understand what each field measures and when to use it.

Consider the following information when using this reference:

  • Metrics represent different types of values, such as percentages, counts, or durations, and are listed in the tables on this page in parentheses in the Type column. This is most relevant when you include multiple metrics in a report's visualization, because you can display only 2 types of metric value in a single visualization. Learn more about including multiple metrics in visualizations.
  • Fields that come from your store's apps and custom data aren't listed on this page, because they're specific to your store. Learn more about using app events and metafields in your reports.

Sidekick

You can ask Sidekick which metrics and dimensions answer a question about your store. Sidekick can query your sales, sessions, customers, payments, payouts, fulfillments, and web performance data. Use a prompt such as Which metric shows my average order value by month?.

Top 30 most helpful fields

Explore your data in new ways with these commonly used fields. These cover the essential metrics and dimensions most merchants need for day-to-day analytics.

Explore your data in new ways with these commonly used fields. These cover the essential metrics and dimensions most merchants need for day-to-day analytics.
NameDescriptionUsesNotesType
Net salesSales revenue, with discounts and sales reversals factored in
Formula: gross sales - discounts - sales reversals
  • Track your revenue after all adjustments and sales reversals.
  • Compare revenue performance across products and time periods after all adjustments.
Best approximation of actual revenue. Preferred over gross_sales for most analyses.Metric (Money total)
Gross salesSales revenue, before discounts and sales reversals are factored in
  • Track your revenue potential before any adjustments.
  • Compare full-price performance across products and time periods.
Full price before any adjustments. Use to understand demand at full price.Metric (Money total)
Total salesAmount customers spent in your store (subtotal, discounts, taxes, fees, shipping, sales reversals)
Formula: net sales + additional fees + duties + shipping charges + taxes
  • Track the complete revenue impact including all fees and adjustments.
  • Compare total customer spending across different products and channels.
The complete amount customers paid, including taxes and shipping. Use for cash flow planning.Metric (Money total)
OrdersNumber of orders placed
  • Track order volume trends to plan inventory and staffing needs.
  • Compare order frequency across different marketing channels and campaigns.
Returns generate order records to maintain accurate inventory and financial tracking. Filter by 'Order status' to exclude returned orders from your analyses.Metric (Count)
Average order valueAverage value of orders placed, excluding any post-order adjustments
Formula: (gross sales - discounts) / orders
  • Increase revenue by focusing on strategies that raise average order value.
  • Set minimum order thresholds for free shipping and promotions.
Revenue ÷ orders. Use to set minimum thresholds for free shipping.Metric (Money average)
Gross profitSales revenue minus the cost of goods sold
Formula: net sales - cost of goods sold
  • Focus marketing and inventory investment on your most profitable products.
  • Set pricing strategies that maximize profit rather than just revenue.
Requires cost of goods sold to be set up in Shopify for accurate calculations.Metric (Money total)
Gross marginPercentage of your sales that is profit (factoring in cost of goods sold)
Formula: gross profit / net sales
  • Focus marketing and inventory investments on higher-margin areas.
  • Set minimum margin requirements for new products and pricing decisions.
Requires cost of goods sold. Use as filter (such as margin < 20%) to find low-margin products.Metric (Percentage & rate)
CustomersNumber of customers who placed an order
  • Track customer acquisition and retention across different time periods.
  • Set customer acquisition goals and budget allocation based on historical performance.
 Metric (Count)
New customersNumber of new customers who placed an order
  • Track customer acquisition performance across marketing channels.
  • Set customer acquisition goals and measure marketing campaign success.
First-time purchasers only. Use to measure acquisition effectiveness.Metric (Count)
Returning customersNumber of returning customers who placed an order
  • Track customer retention success and loyalty program effectiveness.
  • Focus retention marketing on bringing back previous customers.
Customers who've purchased before. Key indicator of loyalty.Metric (Count)
Returning customer ratePercentage of returning customers relative to all customers who placed orders
Formula: returning customers / customers
  • Gauge how well you're retaining customers versus attracting new ones.
  • Decide whether to focus marketing efforts on retention or acquisition.
Higher rates reduce acquisition costs. Most stores display 20-40%.Metric (Percentage & rate)
SessionsNumber of online store visits
  • Track how many times visitors browse your online store.
  • Measure the effectiveness of your marketing campaigns.
Only counted when visitors consent to cookies through your cookie banner. If counts seem low, then verify your cookie banner is displaying and functioning correctly. Note: other analytics platforms calculate sessions differently.Metric (Count)
Online store visitorsUnique visitors (one visitor can visit multiple times)
  • Track how many different people discover your online store.
  • Measure your reach versus repeat visits.
Unique visitors - one person visiting 5 times counts as 1 visitor but 5 sessions.Metric (Count)
Conversion ratePercentage of online store visits (sessions) that resulted in a sale
Formula: sessions that completed checkout / sessions
  • Track how well your online store turns browsers into customers.
  • Set benchmarks for converting visitors into customers.
Might appear lower than expected due to bot traffic. Filter by 'Human' traffic for a more accurate view of actual customer behavior.Metric (Percentage & rate)
Bounce ratePercentage of online store visits that ended after a single pageview
Formula: bounces / sessions
  • Measure how well your online store keeps visitors engaged.
  • Fix landing pages with high bounce rates.
High bounce rate isn't always bad - it might mean visitors found what they needed quickly.Metric (Percentage & rate)
Average session durationAverage duration, in seconds, of online store visits
  • Set targets for how long visitors should spend on your online store.
  • Compare visit length across different time periods.
Measured in seconds. Longer isn't always better - depends on your store type.Metric (Avg duration (seconds))
PageviewsTotal pageviews across all online store visits
  • Track how much content visitors view on your online store.
  • Identify which pages attract the most visitor attention.
 Metric (Count)
Added to cart rateOnline store visits with items added to cart relative to total visits
Formula: sessions with cart additions / sessions
  • Review what percentage of visitors indicate serious buying interest.
  • Improve product pages if too few visitors add items to cart.
Checkouts can exceed add-to-cart counts when customers purchase directly from channels such as Instagram Shopping or Facebook Shops without visiting your cart page.Metric (Percentage & rate)
Reached checkout rateOnline store visits that reached checkout relative to total visits
Formula: sessions that reached checkout / sessions
  • Track what percentage of visitors make it to checkout.
  • Improve your cart and product pages if too few visitors reach checkout.
Checkouts can exceed add-to-cart counts when customers purchase directly from channels such as Instagram Shopping or Facebook Shops without visiting your cart page.Metric (Percentage & rate)
Sessions with cart additionsOnline store visits in which a visitor added an item to cart
  • Track how many visitors indicate serious buying interest.
  • Send cart abandonment emails to visitors who don't complete their purchase.
Use as filter to analyze only high-intent visitors.Metric (Count)
Sessions that completed checkoutOnline store visits in which a purchase was completed
  • Track successful sales from browsing visits.
  • Compare conversion rates across different time periods.
 Metric (Count)
Net items soldNumber of items in the given sale, with reversed quantity factored in
  • Understand your true sales volume by seeing how many ordered items customers kept.
  • Plan inventory replenishment based on net items moving out of stock.
 Metric (Count)
Quantity orderedNumber of items ordered, excluding reversed quantity
  • Track initial demand for products before returns impact the data.
  • Plan inventory levels based on ordering patterns before returns.
Total units ordered, excluding reversed quantity. Useful for inventory planning.Metric (Count)
Reversed quantityNumber of items returned for the given sale
  • Account for expected returns during inventory planning.
  • Identify products, customer segments, or order attributes with high return rates.
 Metric (Count)
Product titleDisplay name of the product that your customers view
  • Focus your marketing budget on the product names that sell best.
  • Rewrite low-performing product titles to improve click-through rates and conversions.
'Product title' displays the current name in your catalog. 'Product title at time of sale' preserves the historical name when the order was placed, which is useful when product names change over time.Dimension
Product variant titleDisplay name of the product variant
  • Review your most popular variants and use them for your marketing.
  • Refine your product and inventory strategy based on what variants sell best.
Specific size/color/style. Use for granular inventory analysis.Dimension
UTM sourceUTM source of the campaign that led to the online store visit
  • Track which traffic sources from your campaigns perform best.
  • Focus marketing spend on sources that drive quality traffic.
Where traffic came from (google, facebook, newsletter). Requires UTM tagging.Dimension
UTM campaignUTM name of the campaign that led to the online store visit
  • Track which campaigns drive the most traffic to your online store.
  • Compare conversion rates across different campaign types.
Which campaign drove the traffic. Requires consistent UTM naming conventions.Dimension
Referrer sourceReferrer type that led to the online store visit (organic, email, and others)
  • Focus marketing budget on the channels that drive the most traffic.
  • Compare conversion rates across different traffic sources.
Automatically detected traffic source. More reliable than UTM for organic traffic.Dimension
New or returning customerLabel specifying whether an order is from a new or returning customer
  • Segment marketing campaigns based on customer purchase history.
  • Track the balance between customer acquisition and retention efforts.
Use as filter to compare new vs returning customer behavior.Dimension

NameDescriptionUsesNotesType

Sessions and behavior

Store traffic and visitor journeys, including page views and browsing patterns.

Note

The Shopify Analytics session measurement rollout runs from September 21 to 23, 2026. When the update reaches your store, your sessions, conversion rate, and other session-based metrics might be different in your reports. This doesn't necessarily mean that your traffic, orders, or customer behavior changed. Learn more about Changes to sessions and conversion rate in Shopify Analytics.

Table containing a list of all sessions and behavior analytics fields.
NameDescriptionUsesNotesType
Added to cart rateOnline store visits with items added to cart relative to total visits
Formula: sessions with cart additions / sessions
  • Review what percentage of visitors indicate serious buying interest.
  • Improve product pages if too few visitors add items to cart.
Checkouts can exceed add-to-cart counts when customers purchase directly from channels such as Instagram Shopping or Facebook Shops without visiting your cart page.Metric (Percentage & rate)
Average session durationAverage duration, in seconds, of online store visits
  • Set targets for how long visitors should spend on your online store.
  • Compare visit length across different time periods.
Measured in seconds. Longer isn't always better - depends on your store type.Metric (Avg duration (seconds))
Bounce ratePercentage of online store visits that ended after a single pageview
Formula: bounces / sessions
  • Measure how well your online store keeps visitors engaged.
  • Fix landing pages with high bounce rates.
High bounce rate isn't always bad - it might mean visitors found what they needed quickly.Metric (Percentage & rate)
BouncesOnline store visits that ended after a single pageview
  • Find visitors who leave immediately after arriving.
  • Improve landing pages that cause visitors to leave quickly.
